easy.def: A dip made from mashed avocado.
examples: We ate guacamole.
The guacamole is green.
I like guacamole with chips.

more.def: A thick green dip made by mashing avocados with onion, lime and spices.
examples: We dipped chips in the guacamole.
Mom mashed the avocados to make guacamole.
The guacamole was green and creamy.

easy.def: A promise that something will work.
examples: The toy has a guarantee.
The guarantee is for one year.
The watch has a guarantee.

more.def: A promise that a product will work well or that something will happen.
examples: The toy has a one-year guarantee.
The store gave a guarantee of fresh bread.
The guarantee says we can return it.

easy.def: To promise.
examples: I guarantee it will work.
The store guarantees the toy.
I guarantee you will like it.

more.def: To promise firmly that something will happen or work.
examples: I guarantee you will like the soup.
The company guarantees the bike for a year.
I cannot guarantee that it will not rain.

easy.def: To keep watch so nothing bad happens.
examples: Dogs guard the house.
He guards the gate.
A big dog guarded the sheep.

more.def: To watch over a person, place or thing to keep it safe.
examples: A dog guards the farm at night.
Soldiers guard the old fort.
The goalie guards the net.

easy.def: A person who keeps a place safe.
examples: The guard stood at the door.
A guard checked our bags.
The guard waved.

more.def: A person whose job is to protect a person or place.
examples: A guard stood at the museum door.
The royal guard wore red coats.
The guard checked everyone's ticket.

easy.def: A small building for a guard.
examples: The guard sat in the guardhouse.
A guardhouse is at the gate.
The guardhouse is small.

more.def: A small building at a gate or entrance where a guard stays.
examples: The guard sat in the guardhouse at the gate.
We showed our tickets at the guardhouse.
A light shone in the guardhouse window.

easy.def: A person who takes care of a child.
examples: My guardian picked me up.
Her guardian signed the form.
A guardian takes care of a child.

more.def: A person who is responsible for taking care of someone else, such as a child.
examples: My guardian signed the permission form.
Her guardians are her aunt and uncle.
The dog is the family's loyal guardian.

easy.def: To give an answer when you are not sure.
examples: Can you guess what is in the box?
I guess you are six years old.
Guess which hand has the coin.

more.def: To give an answer or opinion without knowing for certain.
examples: I guessed that there were two hundred beans in the jar.
Can you guess the ending of the story?
I did not know the answer, so I had to guess.

easy.def: A person who visits.
examples: We have a guest.
The guest sat down.
Guests came to the party.

more.def: A person who is invited to visit or stay somewhere.
examples: We set an extra place for our guest.
The guests arrived at six.
The hotel guest asked for a towel.

easy.def: A small house for visitors.
examples: We stayed in a guesthouse.
The guesthouse is small.
The guesthouse is by the yard.

more.def: A small house or building where visitors can stay.
examples: We stayed in the guesthouse behind the main house.
The guesthouse had two beds.
A cozy guesthouse sat by the garden.

easy.def: Help with what to do.
examples: I need guidance.
The teacher gave guidance.
Thank you for your guidance.

more.def: Advice or help that shows you the way.
examples: The teacher gave guidance on the project.
I needed guidance finding the book.
Under her guidance, the team improved.

easy.def: To show someone the way.
examples: The lights guide the ships.
Mom guides the baby's hand.
A map will guide us.

more.def: To lead or show the way to someone.
examples: A ranger guided us along the trail to the waterfall.
The stars guided sailors across the sea long ago.
A helper guided the new student to her classroom.

easy.def: A book that tells you about a place.
examples: We read the guidebook.
The guidebook has maps.
I packed a guidebook.

more.def: A book that gives information about a place for people who visit it.
examples: We read the guidebook before our trip to the city.
The guidebook showed us where to eat.
A guidebook told us about the park's trails.

easy.def: A rule or tip that helps you do something.
examples: Follow the guideline.
A guideline for the contest.
The guideline is simple.

more.def: A rule or piece of advice that tells you how to do something the right way.
examples: Follow the guideline on the sign: no running by the pool.
The teacher gave us guidelines for the project.
The guidelines say that your essay should be one page long.

easy.def: A bad feeling that you did something wrong.
examples: I felt guilt about the lie.
She had a lot of guilt.
Guilt made him tell the truth.

more.def: A feeling of shame or sorrow that you get when you know you did something wrong.
examples: He felt guilt after telling a lie.
Guilt made her tell the truth.
The guilt over the broken vase stayed with her.

easy.def: Feeling bad because you did something wrong.
examples: I feel guilty about the mess.
He felt guilty.
She looked guilty.

more.def: Feeling ashamed because you know you did something wrong.
examples: I felt guilty when I ate the last cookie.
The dog looked guilty beside the torn pillow.
She felt guilty for forgetting her friend's birthday.

easy.def: A musical instrument with strings.
examples: I play the guitar.
He strums the guitar.
The guitar has six strings.

more.def: A musical instrument with a long neck and strings that you pluck or strum.
examples: She played the guitar and sang.
He strummed the guitar by the campfire.
A guitar usually has six strings.

easy.def: A person who plays the guitar.
examples: The guitarist played.
A guitarist sang.
He is a guitarist.

more.def: A person who plays the guitar.
examples: The guitarist strummed a happy song.
A guitarist joined the band.
She is the best guitarist in school.

easy.def: A large part of the sea that reaches into the land.
examples: The boat sailed across the gulf.
We swam in the gulf.
The gulf is warm.

more.def: A large area of sea that is partly enclosed by land.
examples: Many shrimp boats work in the warm waters of the gulf.
A ferry took us across the gulf to the island.
Dolphins swim in the gulf near the coast.

easy.def: A very big space between two things.
examples: There is a gulf between them.
A deep gulf was in the ground.
The gulf felt wide.

more.def: A very wide gap or difference between two people or ideas.
examples: There was a gulf between the two friends after their quarrel.
A wide gulf separated the old way of farming from the new.
The canyon was a deep gulf that we could not cross.

easy.def: A white bird that lives near the sea.
examples: A gull flew by.
The gull ate fish.
We heard gulls.

more.def: A white and gray sea bird with a loud cry that eats fish and scraps of food; also called a seagull.
examples: A gull glided over the harbor and landed on the pier.
The gull screamed as it chased the fishing boat.
We fed the gulls on the beach.

easy.def: Easy to trick.
examples: The gullible boy believed the joke.
She is gullible.
Do not be gullible.

more.def: Too quick to believe things, and so easy to trick.
examples: The gullible boy believed his brother's silly story.
She is so gullible that she believed the moon was cheese.
Do not be gullible: check if a claim is true.

easy.def: A narrow ditch made by running water.
examples: We walked in the gully.
Water runs in the gully.
The gully is deep.

more.def: A narrow valley or ditch cut by running water.
examples: Rain water ran down the gully.
We jumped across the narrow gully.
The old gully was dry in summer.

easy.def: To swallow fast in big bites or sips.
examples: I gulp my water when I am hot.
The dog gulped his food.
Do not gulp your milk.

more.def: To swallow food or drink quickly in large amounts.
examples: After the race, she gulped down a whole glass of water.
The hungry puppy gulped its dinner in seconds.
He gulped the cold juice and sighed.

easy.def: A big swallow.
examples: He took a big gulp of milk.
She drank it in one gulp.
I took a gulp of air.

more.def: One large swallow of food, drink or air.
examples: He drank the lemonade in two big gulps.
She took a gulp of air before diving underwater.
With one nervous gulp, he walked onto the stage.

easy.def: A sweet candy that you chew but do not swallow.
examples: I chew gum.
The gum is sticky.
Do not swallow your gum.

more.def: A soft, chewy treat that you chew and do not swallow.
examples: I chewed gum on the bus.
The gum stuck to my shoe.
The gum lost its flavor.

easy.def: The pink part of your mouth around your teeth.
examples: My gums are pink.
The dentist checked my gums.
I brush my gums.

more.def: The firm, pink flesh around the bottom of your teeth.
examples: My gums were a little sore.
The dentist checked my teeth and gums.
Brushing helps keep your gums healthy.

easy.def: Sticky and chewy.
examples: The candy is gummy.
A gummy bear.
The gummy bread stuck.

more.def: Sticky and chewy like gum.
examples: The gummy candy stuck to my teeth.
She ate a gummy bear.
The dough turned gummy.

easy.def: A tool that shoots small metal balls.
examples: A gun is loud.
The police have a gun.
He saw a gun in the museum.

more.def: A weapon that shoots bullets, which can hurt people and animals.
examples: The museum has an old gun from long ago.
A police officer carries a gun for work.
On the old farm, a gun hung over the fireplace.

easy.def: To flow out fast and a lot.
examples: Water gushed out.
The pipe gushed.
Blood gushed from the cut.

more.def: To flow out in a fast and strong stream, or to talk with too much excitement.
examples: Water gushed from the broken pipe.
The fountain gushed high into the air.
She gushed about how much she loved the gift.

easy.def: A sudden strong wind.
examples: A gust of wind came.
The gust blew my hat off.
There was a gust.

more.def: A sudden, strong rush of wind.
examples: A gust of wind blew my hat off.
A strong gust shook the windows.
Gusts of wind made the kite dance.

easy.def: The long tube inside your belly where food goes.
examples: The food goes into your gut.
The gut is long.
Doctors look at the gut.

more.def: The long tube in the body where food is broken down, or the belly.
examples: Food moves through your gut as it is digested.
A healthy gut helps you digest food.
The doctor pressed on his gut.

easy.def: The tubes inside the belly.
examples: The doctor looked at the guts.
The guts digest food.
The fish was cleaned of its guts.

more.def: The tubes in the middle of the body where food is digested.
examples: The fisherman cleaned the fish and took out its guts.
The guts of an animal break down the food it eats.
A snake's guts are long and thin.

easy.def: Courage.
examples: It takes guts to jump.
She has guts.
He had the guts to speak up.

more.def: Courage, or the strength to do something that is hard or scary.
examples: It took guts to speak in front of the whole school.
She had the guts to try the high diving board.
He showed guts when he stood up to the bully.

easy.def: A channel that carries rain away.
examples: Rain runs down the gutter.
The gutter is full of leaves.
Dad cleaned the gutter.

more.def: A long, narrow channel along a roof or street that carries away rainwater.
examples: Rain ran down the gutter.
The gutter on the roof was full of leaves.
The ball rolled into the gutter.

easy.def: A boy or a man.
examples: That guy has a big dog.
The guy at the shop was nice.
He is a funny guy.

more.def: A boy or man, in everyday talk, or a friendly way to speak to a group.
examples: The guy who drives the school bus knows all our names.
He is a friendly guy who loves to tell jokes.
Come on, guys, it is time to go!
